channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario was warned of 'suspicious' OSAP activity at a few career colleges: documents
Ontario's top court rejects developer’s constitutional challenge over Greenbelt law
item.description: The Ontario Court of Appeal has sided with a lower court in rejecting a developer’s constitutional challenge of a 2023 law that returned 15 parcels of land to the Greenbelt.

item.title: Legal groups in court today to challenge Ontario’s new cash bail system
item.description: Ontario’s new rules requiring a cash deposit for bail encroach on federal jurisdiction and will make it harder for people to be released as they await trial, two legal organizations argued Thursday as they asked the court to scrap the regulations.

item.title: Husband of Ontario MPP sells shares in airline that carries out Trump deportations
item.description: The husband of an MPP appointed to support Ontario’s attorney general has sold his shares in an airline that has been accused of being part of a system that violates the rights of detainees. The airline proceeds with the Trump administration’s controversial deportation flights more than any other carrier.

item.title: ‘We’re always going to call it Lake Ontario,’ Ford says after Trump threatened to rename it ‘Lake America’
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he is considering changing the name of Lake Ontario amid the ongoing trade dispute between the U.S. and Canada.

item.title: Ontario government takes next step towards possible nuclear plant on America’s doorstep
item.description: The Ontario government has taken the next step towards a potential nuclear power plant south of Sarnia, Ont., that could bring thousands of permanent and construction jobs.

item.title: Doug Ford says it’s time to turn down the temperature one day after calling Donald Trump ‘a loser’
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says that it is time to turn down the temperature after “things got a little heated” and a “little personal” with U.S. President Donald Trump one day prior.

item.title: Ontario students brace for 'vast amount' of debt amid OSAP changes, tuition increases
item.description: As Aidan Jeffers begins his graduate studies at the University of Toronto, he says he will have to work more hours and possibly rely on food banks due to drastic changes to student financial aid in Ontario – and the resulting debt he expects to rack up.

item.title: ‘Loser’ and ‘King of bankruptcies:’ This is everything Doug Ford said about Donald Trump amid war of words
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford is slamming Donald Trump as a "dictator" and the "king of bankruptcies" after the U.S. president criticized him on social media on Monday afternoon.

item.title: Ford wants Ontario to hit back after Trump’s latest tariffs on Canada
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford is doubling down on Prime Minister Mark Carney’s decision to suspend trade negotiations with the United States, saying Canada must respond forcefully after new U.S. tariffs took effect Saturday.

item.title: Nominations to run in Ontario’s fall municipal elections now closed
item.description: Ontarians now have a clearer picture of the choices they’ll face at the ballot box this fall, with nominations for thousands of municipal roles locked down after a final burst of declarations.

item.title: Ontario raises speed limits on several highways effective Friday, including stretches of Hwy. 400
item.description: Drivers across the province will soon be able to travel faster as speed limits increase on numerous highways, including some stretches of Hwy. 400.

item.title: Ontario teachers will be without a contract as school returns but education minister ‘very optimistic’
item.description: Ontario’s education minister says he’s hopeful the province can strike a deal with all of its teachers and education workers unions, pledging that schools will open “as usual” after Labour Day.

item.title: Ontario teachers’ union slams ‘broken system’ that they say has stalled talks on new contract
item.description: The union representing Ontario’s secondary school teachers is calling for the repeal of a “broken system” that it says has stalled negotiations weeks prior to the expiration of teacher contracts.

item.title: RBC names former Ontario cabinet minister Caroline Mulroney as vice-chair
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada has hired Caroline Mulroney as vice chair and she is to report to Derek Neldner, the head of capital markets, starting Sept. 14.
